newsitem.title: NORWAY: BP takes first sample from Norway deepwater.
newsitem.headline: BP takes first sample from Norway deepwater.

text.p: British Petroleum Norge said on Wednesday it had encountered a reservoir and taken a sample from the first deep water well in the frontier area, Nyk High, in the Norwegian Sea.
The well 6707/10-1 lies in a water depth of 1,270 metres and is the first deep water spud on the Norwegian continental shelf.
"We have successfully encountered a reservoir and recovered the first fluid sample, which is on its way to Stavanger for analysis," said BP spokesman Ole Helgesen.
"We will not have any indication (of the reservoir content) for another week or so," he said.
The Norwegian Oil Directorate is charged with releasing any results of drilling in Norwegian waters.
BP plans to drill through the reservoir down to a total depth of about 5,000 metres below sea level, which will take another two to three weeks, Helgesen said.
BP, in partnership with Saga Petroleum ASA, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS and Esso, was awarded the Nykhoegda deepwater licence PL218 in Norway's 15th licencing round last year.
